# Urdu Dua & Ruqyah

Produce idiomatic, dignified Urdu across the complete database. A filled target is not automatically a good translation, and a completed `duas` table is not a completed database.

## Required context

Before changing translations, read:

- [references/project-scope.md](references/project-scope.md) for every required table, source, field, and completion gate.
- [references/urdu-style.md](references/urdu-style.md) for the Urdu register and review standard.

## Start and finish with status

```powershell
python scripts/work_status.py --workspace "G:\dua-ruqyah\dua_main_ur_translation" --write
```

Run it from this skill directory, or pass the script's absolute path. It writes `WORK_STATUS.md` in the Urdu workspace and exposes required tables missing from the current chunk index. Do not report the percentage for the partial index as whole-project completion.

## Translation workflow

1. Identify the first incomplete or omitted required table from `WORK_STATUS.md`.
2. If scope is missing, add chunks and metadata for only those missing tables. Do not run a destructive generator over translated files.
3. Translate one manageable chunk at a time. Edit only target text and permitted status/review metadata.
4. Read English and Bengali context when both exist. Follow the source routing in `project-scope.md`; resolve a real conflict from Arabic or the cited primary text and record the decision in `GLOSSARY.json` overrides.
5. Translate nested `duas.groups` and structured `drawer_items.content`; these are user-visible text.
6. Run `python scripts/verify.py <chunk>` from the Urdu workspace. Correct every error.
7. Perform a separate naturalness pass against `urdu-style.md`. Mark a chunk done only after semantic, structural, and Urdu-quality review.
8. Update `PLAN.md` where it already tracks the chunk, and regenerate `WORK_STATUS.md`. Status must come from the files, not optimistic prose.

Do not silently alter Arabic, IDs, keys, links, audio, counts, HTML structure, reference numbers, transliteration, or nullness. Inline and top-level references remain normalized English with ASCII digits. Preserve all source numbers, converting Bengali/Arabic digit glyphs to ASCII without changing their values.

## Completion and build gate

Never build or say ├óΓé¼┼ôcomplete├óΓé¼┬¥ while any of these is true:

- a required text-bearing table is absent from the work index;
- any target or nested target is blank;
- a chunk has not passed structural verification and a natural-Urdu review;

- glossary spellings, honorifics, names, numbers, Arabic, HTML, keys, or nullness are inconsistent;
- books, book details, sections, drawer screens, or nested dua groups were excluded;
- final row counts/schema differ from their routed source tables.

When all gates pass, run the full verifier and build without `--partial`:

```powershell
python scripts/verify.py
python scripts/build.py ur
```

Then require `PRAGMA integrity_check = ok`, compare every table's row count and primary-key set with its designated source, scan all user-visible fields for Bengali residue and blank targets, and record the database path and verification date in `WORK_STATUS.md`.

# Natural Urdu standard

Write contemporary, educated Pakistani Urdu suitable for worship, guidance, and general app screens. It should sound authored in Urdu, not converted sentence by sentence from English or Bengali.

## Voice

- Use calm, respectful, devotional language without artificial grandeur.
- Prefer familiar, flowing Urdu sentence order. Break unwieldy source sentences where meaning and markup permit.
- Address the reader consistently and respectfully; avoid casual `├ÿ┬¬├ÖΓÇª` unless a quoted source requires it.
- Use idiomatic verbs and complete predicates. Avoid noun-heavy calques and English-style passive chains.
- Use common Urdu vocabulary where it is precise. Retain established Islamic Arabic terms rather than replacing them with Hindi/Sanskrit or awkward explanatory phrases.
- Do not add sermons, rulings, praise, or explanations absent from the source.

## Religious wording

- Use `├ÿ┬º├ÖΓÇ₧├ÖΓÇ₧├¢┬ü` consistently, not variant spellings.
- Use `├ÿ┬»├ÿ┬╣├ÿ┬º`, `├ÿ┬░├Ü┬⌐├ÿ┬▒`, `├ÿ┬º├ÿ┬░├Ü┬⌐├ÿ┬º├ÿ┬▒`, `├ÖΓÇá├ÖΓÇª├ÿ┬º├ÿ┬▓`, `├ÿ┬▒├Ü┬⌐├Ö╦å├ÿ┬╣`, `├ÿ┬│├ÿ┬¼├ÿ┬»├¢┬ü`, `├ÿ┬¬├Ö╦å├ÿ┬¿├¢┬ü`, `├ÿ┬º├ÿ┬│├ÿ┬¬├ÿ┬║├Ö┬ü├ÿ┬º├ÿ┬▒`, `├ÿ┬▒├ÖΓÇÜ├¢┼Æ├¢┬ü` according to the glossary.
- Preserve established honorifics accurately: `├ÿ┬▒├ÿ┬│├Ö╦å├ÖΓÇ₧ ├ÿ┬º├ÖΓÇ₧├ÖΓÇ₧├¢┬ü ├»┬╖┬║`, `├ÿ┬▒├ÿ┬╢├¢┼Æ ├ÿ┬º├ÖΓÇ₧├ÖΓÇ₧├¢┬ü ├ÿ┬╣├ÖΓÇá├¢┬ü/├ÿ┬╣├ÖΓÇá├¢┬ü├ÿ┬º/├ÿ┬╣├ÖΓÇá├¢┬ü├ÖΓÇª├ÿ┬º`, `├ÿ┬▒├ÿ┬¡├ÖΓÇª├¢┬ü ├ÿ┬º├ÖΓÇ₧├ÖΓÇ₧├¢┬ü`, and `├ÿ┬╣├ÖΓÇ₧├¢┼Æ├¢┬ü ├ÿ┬º├ÖΓÇ₧├ÿ┬│├ÖΓÇ₧├ÿ┬º├ÖΓÇª`. Attach them only to the correct person.
- Use established Urdu spellings for prophets, Companions, scholars, surahs, collections, and places. Keep one spelling throughout.
- Translate the meaning of Quran/hadith prose faithfully while leaving Arabic fields and Arabic blocks untouched.

## Human-quality rejection signs

Rewrite text that has any of these traits:

- source-language word order, repeated pronouns, or stiff literal connectors;
- unnecessary English words when natural Urdu exists;
- Bengali script or Bengali grammatical structure;
- mixed respectful and casual address;
- incorrect gender, number, agreement, postpositions, or compound verbs;
- excessive Persianized formality that obscures a simple source;
- machine-like repetition, fragmented clauses, or untranslated labels;
- a title that names a different action/person/time from its content;
- numbers interpreted as dates, ages, or quantities not present in the source.

## Review aloud

After semantic comparison, read each target as continuous Urdu without looking at the source. It must be immediately understandable, grammatically complete, and natural when spoken. Then compare again with the source to ensure fluency did not remove qualifications, negation, speakers, references, or repetitions.

Keep ASCII digits in references and technical identifiers. Keep inline citations in normalized English unless the project glossary explicitly defines a different approved presentation.

    "duas.content.390": "English wrongly introduces the displayed text as the prayer tashahhud. The supplied text is Khutbat al-Hajah, as Bengali says. Preserve the initial mention of both teachings but introduce the correct displayed passage.",
    "duas.translation.390": "English omits the kinship clause from Quran 4:1. Supplied Arabic wal-arham and Bengali both include it; Urdu restores it without altering citation numbers.",
    "duas.translation.394": "English and Bengali mistranslate the final clause as gathering or separating good things. Supplied Arabic asks Allah to keep the spouses together in goodness for as long as He joins them, and to separate them in goodness if He separates them.",
    "duas.translation.412": "English omits by Your favour, which is explicit in the supplied Arabic bifadlika and Bengali. Urdu preserves this phrase.",
    "duas.translation.416": "English repeats the grave trial and says wash my sins. Supplied Arabic and Bengali have one grave-trial clause and ask to wash the heart with snow and hail water. Urdu follows those without the English duplication.",
    "duas.translation.417": "English omits Lord of the earth, which appears in the supplied Arabic and Bengali. Restore it in Urdu and render the present grasp of the forelock rather than the English future tense.",
    "duas.note.365": "English reverses the wording of the hypothetical regret. Bengali and Muslim 2664 say if I had done such-and-such, this would have happened. Urdu preserves that conditional form.",
    "duas.note.381": "The prose omits the speaker. Musnad Ahmad 712 explicitly has Ali reporting that the Prophet addressed him; restore that attribution. Retain the unusual already-forgiven wording, which really occurs in the Arabic. Checked the Musnad text reproduced at https://dorar.net/h/JcEng0hJ?osoul=1 .",
    "duas.content.394": "The cited Adab al-Zifaf discusses a raised report but explicitly prefers the version stopping at Ibn Masud. Attribute this instruction to Ibn Masud rather than unconditionally to the Prophet; frozen reference remains unchanged. Checked https://islamhouse.com/read/ar/????-??????-??-?????-???????-276162 , section 2, footnote to the second report.",
    "duas.note.397": "The supplied claim about Companions conflicts with the Hasan al-Basri attribution in row 396 and the Nawawi recommendation for the reply in row 362. Urdu uses the accurate broader attribution to scholars; see Hisn al-Muslim chapter 47, https://risala.prh.gov.sa/storage/contents/51/ar_hisnulmuslim.pdf .",
    "duas.note.428": "English reverses the hypothetical by saying 'if I had not done that'. The supplied Arabic in Muslim 2664 says law anni fa'altu, and Bengali likewise says 'if I had done'; Urdu follows that wording, consistent with row 365. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2664 .",
    "duas.content.445": "English says Allah will forgive the debt. Bengali says He will free the person from debt, which is the intended meaning in this debt-settlement context; Urdu says Allah will grant release from debt.",
    "duas.translation.451": "English paraphrases wallahu hasibuhu as Allah knowing the exact truth. The supplied Arabic literally makes Allah the person's Reckoner; Urdu preserves that meaning.",
    "duas.group_items.453.1.content": "The malformed English changes the addressee and speaker. Muslim 2346 has people asking Abdullah ibn Sarjis whether the Messenger sought forgiveness for him; Abdullah answers yes, for them too, and recites the verse. Urdu restores those speakers. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2346 .",
    "duas.content.458": "English compresses Sa'd's offer into half his family and property. Bukhari 5167 says Sa'd ibn al-Rabi offered half his property and one of his two wives after divorce; Urdu states the actual offer without the misleading half-family wording. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5167 .",
    "duas.note.458": "English gives two awkward alternatives for the mahr. Bukhari 5167 states gold equal to the weight of a date stone; Urdu uses that exact meaning. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5167 .",
    "duas.content.463": "English accidentally repeats returning the greeting, creating six rights after announcing five. Bengali and Bukhari 1240 contain exactly five; Urdu removes the duplicate and preserves those five. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1240 .",
    "duas.content.469": "English is grammatically malformed and makes the listener the possible speaker. Tirmidhi 2741 explicitly instructs the person who sneezes to say this praise; Urdu restores that speaker. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2741 .",
    "duas.content.471": "English is grammatically malformed and appears to make the sneezer say yarhamukallah. Tirmidhi 2741 has another person say it to the sneezer, who then gives the displayed reply; Urdu makes the exchange explicit. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2741 .",
    "duas.translation.478": "As in row 451, supplied Arabic wallahu hasibuhu makes Allah the person's Reckoner. Urdu preserves that wording instead of the looser English paraphrase.",
    "duas.translation.483": "English mistranslates qurbatan as the reward of a sacrificial slaughter. The supplied Arabic, Bengali and Bukhari 6361 say a means of nearness to Allah; Urdu restores that meaning, consistent with row 450. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6361 .",
    "duas.translation.491": "English adds Paradise to 'make it a treasure for me'. The supplied Arabic indaka and Bengali say 'with You'; Urdu follows them. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3424 .",
    "duas.content.492": "English renders Arabic tiratan mechanically as deprivation descending. Bengali gives regret; Urdu uses the natural hadith sense, 'a cause of regret from Allah', for both sitting and lying. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4856 .",
    "duas.translation.494": "English says All-Forgiving, but the supplied Arabic ends al-Rahim and Bengali says Merciful. Urdu therefore uses 'Most Merciful' rather than repeating row 474, whose Arabic ends al-Ghafur.",
    "duas.content.497": "The English ending is badly corrupted. Urdu restores the instruction to eat with the right hand and from what is directly in front, followed by Umar ibn Abi Salamah's statement that he continued eating that way. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5376 .",
    "duas.name.501": "English says the dua is between eating and drinking. Muslim 2734a says Allah is pleased when a servant praises Him after eating food or drinking; Urdu corrects the timing. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2734a .",
    "duas.content.501": "Same timing correction as the title: praise follows eating or drinking, rather than occurring between them. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2734a .",
    "duas.content.511": "English corrupts the opening instruction. Bukhari 3304 says to keep children close when night begins because devils spread, then release them after part of the night has passed; Urdu restores that wording. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3304 .",
    "duas.note.512": "English has the nonsensical phrase 'donkeys of dogs'. Abu Dawud 5103 says dogs barking and donkeys braying at night; Urdu restores both animals and the reason for seeking refuge. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5103 .",
    "duas.translation.513": "English omits la ilaha illa anta, which is present in the supplied Arabic and Bengali. Urdu restores 'there is no deity worthy of worship except You'.",
    "duas.content.516": "English calls the wind Allah's 'liveliness'. Abu Dawud 5097 describes wind as being from Allah's mercy; Urdu follows the hadith. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5097 .",
    "duas.content.518": "English leaves the first-person narrator unnamed. Bukhari 3206 identifies her as Aisha; Urdu names her so the narration and direct address remain clear. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3206 .",
    "duas.translation.523": "English uses 'pardon us' for wa aafina. The supplied Arabic asks for well-being or safety; Urdu uses ├ÿ┬╣├ÿ┬º├Ö┬ü├¢┼Æ├ÿ┬¬ ├ÿ┬╣├ÿ┬╖├ÿ┬º ├Ö┬ü├ÿ┬▒├ÖΓÇª├ÿ┬º.",
    "duas.translation.524": "English mistranslates the opening as reliance. The supplied Arabic la tayra illa tayruka and Bengali concern omens; Urdu states that no omen has effect apart from Allah's decree.",
    "duas.note.524": "English omits the statement that gives the expiation its context. The supplied Bengali and Musnad Ahmad 7045 state that allowing an omen to stop an intended action is shirk; Urdu restores that sentence before the Companions' question.",
    "duas.note.531": "English labels al-Aswad with RA, but al-Aswad ibn Yazid is the intermediary narrator asking Aisha. Urdu uses rahimahullah for him while retaining radiyallahu anha for Aisha. The chain is visible in https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5741 .",
    "duas.translation.535": "English omits bi-idhni rabbina. The supplied Bengali and Bukhari 5745 include healing by permission of our Lord; Urdu restores that clause. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5745 .",
    "duas.group_items.536.0.note": "English says Uthman ibn Abi al-As reported an 'explanation' of his body. Muslim 2202 records his complaint of pain; Urdu restores the complaint and the Prophet's instructions. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2202 .",
    "duas.content.538": "English misidentifies the opening transmitters as Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Layla and his father. The cited Tirmidhi 969 has Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah narrating from his father; Urdu follows that chain and the cited report rather than the extra clauses in Bengali. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:969 .",
    "duas.content.544": "English names only Abu Hurayrah, but Tirmidhi 3430 has al-Agharr Abu Muslim bearing witness from both Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah. Urdu restores both Companion narrators. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3430 .",
    "duas.group_items.544.3.note": "The malformed English makes Allah the speaker of the concluding promise. Tirmidhi 3430 first gives Allah's affirmation, then attributes 'whoever says it during illness...' to the Prophet. Urdu makes both speakers explicit. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3430 .",
    "duas.content.546": "English omits whom to prompt and is grammatically incomplete. Muslim 916a says to prompt those who are dying to recite the declaration of faith; Urdu restores the object. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:916a .",
    "duas.note.4": "Surah occurs only in the inline citation, which remains normalized English under the project rules. Do not add an Urdu surah label solely to satisfy the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.translation.5": "English ends with 'You are upon a straight path', but the supplied Arabic and Bengali say that Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path. Urdu follows them.",
    "duas.translation.9": "English renders wa aafini as 'strengthen me'. The supplied Arabic and Bengali ask for well-being; Urdu correctly uses ├ÿ┬╣├ÿ┬º├Ö┬ü├¢┼Æ├ÿ┬¬.",
    "duas.translation.11": "English begins 'O Allah', but the supplied Arabic says Rabbi and Bengali likewise addresses 'my Lord'. Urdu follows the actual invocation: ├ÿ┬º├¢ΓÇÖ ├ÖΓÇª├¢┼Æ├ÿ┬▒├¢ΓÇÖ ├ÿ┬▒├ÿ┬¿.",
    "duas.note.13": "English renders dandanah as reciting beautifully. Ibn Majah 910 describes the man's inability to make the Prophet's and Muadh's detailed supplications and the reply that their supplication revolves around seeking Paradise and refuge from Hell; Urdu restores that sense. Checked https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:910 .",
    "duas.content.14": "English says one day, but the supplied Bengali says after some days and the Arabic of Tirmidhi 3514 has ayyaman. Urdu uses 'after a few days'. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3514 .",
    "duas.group_items.29.0.translation": "English omits wa aafini, although it is present in the supplied nested Arabic. Urdu restores the request for well-being.",
    "duas.content.30": "English omits that the new Muslim was first taught the prayer. The supplied Bengali and Muslim 2697b include this before the instruction to supplicate; Urdu restores it. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2697b .",
    "duas.translation.30": "English omits wa aafini, which is present in the supplied Arabic, Bengali and Muslim 2697b. Urdu restores 'grant me well-being'. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2697b .",
    "duas.name.254": "Surah occurs only inside the parenthetical Quran citation. The citation remains in English under the project rules, so no Urdu surah label is added solely for the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.translation.281": "Surah occurs only inside the inline Quran citation. The citation remains in English under the project rules, so no Urdu surah label is added solely for the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.note.496": "Tirmidhi occurs only inside the inline hadith citation. The citation remains in English under the project rules, so no Urdu collection name is added solely for the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.content.33": "English incorrectly gives Ibn Qudamah the Companion honorific RA. He is one of the transmitters whose version specifies the right hand; Urdu uses rahimahullah. Checked the chain at https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1502 .",
    "duas.content.38": "English says 'on the last night', but the cited Tirmidhi narration refers to the latter part of the night. Urdu states the intended time clearly.",
    "duas.translation.47": "English loosely says 'take me out of my plight'. The supplied Arabic ajurni fi musibati asks for reward in the calamity, and wakhluf li khayran minha asks for a better replacement; Urdu preserves both clauses.",
    "duas.note.49": "English mechanically renders the Prophet's question as 'such and such a word'. In context he asks who uttered the displayed words; Urdu makes that referent explicit. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:601 .",
    "duas.content.59": "English omits 'and the Prophets before me'. The supplied Bengali and Tirmidhi 3585 both include this clause; Urdu restores it. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3585 .",
    "duas.content.63": "English incorrectly begins with Umm Darda as narrator while continuing in Safwan's first person, and labels Safwan RA. The actual chain has Safwan ibn Abdullah narrating his exchange with Umm Darda; Urdu restores the speaker and uses rahimahullah for Safwan. The same chain is visible at https://sunnah.com/adab/31/22 .",
    "duas.note.65": "English labels the sub-narrator Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr with RA. He is a later transmitter, so Urdu uses rahimahullah. The wording about small girls is retained accurately. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:755 .",
    "duas.content.66": "English says the fasting person's supplication is accepted when he breaks his fast, but the supplied Bengali and the Arabic hatta yuftir in Tirmidhi 3598 say until he breaks his fast. Urdu follows the Arabic timing. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3598 .",
    "duas.name.69": "English calls this the oppressed person's supplication, but the content is Quran 27:62 about the desperate or distressed person. Urdu follows the actual verse subject.",
    "duas.translation.73": "As in row 47, English omits the explicit request for reward in the calamity. The supplied Arabic and Bengali include it; Urdu restores that meaning.",
    "duas.name.77": "English calls this the excellence of dua, but the report itself concerns sitting with people remembering Allah, and Bengali likewise identifies dhikr. Urdu names the actual subject.",
    "duas.translation.83": "English incorrectly asks for the good of this day. The supplied Arabic says hadhihi al-laylah and the evening context requires night; Urdu follows the Arabic.",
    "duas.translation.89": "English incorrectly says All-Seeing. The supplied Arabic al-Sami and the English note both say All-Hearing; Urdu follows the Arabic.",
    "duas.name.93": "English title says morning and evening, but the instruction and report specify reciting this in the morning. Urdu names the actual time.",
    "duas.note.100": "English confuses Abu Bakrah with Abu Bakr and labels his son as a Companion. Abu Dawud 5090 has Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah addressing his father Abu Bakrah; Urdu restores the names and uses rahimahullah for the intermediary. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5090 .",
    "duas.note.111": "English gives only the kunyah Abu Malik. Sahih Muslim 2697b and its narrator chain identify him as Sa'd ibn Tariq al-Ashja'i narrating from his Companion father Tariq ibn Ashyam; Urdu supplies their names and correct honorifics. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2697b and https://sunnah.com/narrator/3248 ."
  },

    "duas.translation.297": "English calls the deceased the son of a male and female servant. The supplied Arabic ├ÿ┬╣├ÿ┬¿├ÿ┬»├Ö╞Æ ├Ö╦å├ÿ┬º├ÿ┬¿├ÖΓÇá ├ÿ┬ú├ÖΓÇª├ÿ┬¬├Ö╞Æ calls him Allah's servant and the son of His female servant; the Bengali supports this, and Urdu follows it.",
    "duas.translation.299": "As in row 295, Arabic wa aafihaa and Bengali mean well-being, not strength. The stray English masculine pronouns refer to the female deceased; Urdu consistently uses the female context.",
    "duas.translation.301": "English calls her the daughter of male and female servants. Supplied Arabic and Bengali call her Allah's female servant and the daughter of His female servant; Urdu follows those.",
    "duas.note.310": "English asks whether to pray on Laylatul Qadr. Bengali asks what supplication to make, which matches the response teaching a particular dua; Urdu follows Bengali.",
    "duas.note.315": "English adultery is too narrow. Bengali describes sexual conduct, and Bukhari 1894 uses la yarfuth; Urdu preserves the broader meaning. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1894 .",
    "duas.translation.316": "English describes past actions, but the Arabic and Bengali are a supplication for the hosts; Urdu retains that prayer form.",
    "duas.name.319": "English title mentions only returning, but the main dua and content concern starting a journey and the nested group adds the return wording. Urdu follows the Bengali title covering both.",
    "duas.translation.321": "English safety represents Arabic amanataka; Bengali explicitly says entrusted responsibility. Urdu uses the established religious term amanat.",
    "duas.note.321": "The explanatory rendering repeats the same amanataka phrase as the main translation; Urdu consistently uses amanat rather than English safety. Embedded Latin transliteration remains verbatim.",
    "duas.name.323": "English title says traveller praying for resident, but the actual dua and note concern arriving or stopping at a place. Urdu follows the Bengali subject; retains English #1.",
    "duas.name.324": "English title says traveller praying for resident, but the actual dua and note concern entering a town. Urdu follows the Bengali subject; retains #2.",
    "duas.content.327": "Abu al-Malih is the intermediary narrator, not the Companion who rode behind the Prophet. Use rahimahullah for him and radiyallahu anhu for the unnamed Companion. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4982 and https://sunnah.com/narrator/4091 .",
    "duas.note.327": "Same narrator attribution and honorific correction as content. Preserve the repeated narration and the note's additional ending.",
    "duas.translation.329": "English capitalizes He Who listens ambiguously. Bengali addresses a hearer, matching Arabic samia samiun; Urdu addresses the listener and does not turn this into a divine name.",
    "duas.note.331": "English says any means of transport, contradicting the boat title and dua. Bengali specifically says land vehicles; Urdu follows that scope while preserving the author's statement.",
    "duas.content.339": "English marks Amr ibn Shuayb as a Companion and vaguely says predecessors. Preserve the chain through his father to his grandfather, use rahimahullah for Amr and radiyallahu anhu for the Companion, and identify preceding prophets as in Bengali and Tirmidhi 3585. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3585 .",
    "duas.note.339": "Same chain, honorific and preceding-prophets correction as content; preserve the repeated narration.",
    "duas.group_items.343.1.note": "English incorrectly inserts (the sky) as the subject and says full fair. This is the Prophet staying until daylight brightens, as the parallel narration in row 340 and Bengali show.",
    "duas.content.347": "Both supplied prose versions corrupt the animal and body-part description. The cited Bukhari 5565 explicitly describes two horned black-and-white rams and placing a foot on their sides. Urdu restores those details. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5565 .",
    "duas.content.352": "Muslim occurs only in the inline citation [Muslim: 780], which the skill requires copying in English. Do not add an Urdu collection name solely to satisfy the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.note.357": "The Uqbah here is Uqbah ibn Muslim, an intermediary narrator in Abu Dawud 466, not the Companion Uqbah ibn Amir. Use rahimahullah rather than the source RA. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:466 .",
    "duas.content.361": "Source Husain (RA) is an attribution error. Hisn al-Muslim attributes these words to Hasan al-Basri; Urdu uses Hasan Basri rahimahullah. Checked https://risala.prh.gov.sa/storage/contents/51/ar_hisnulmuslim.pdf . The frozen Abu Dawood: 441 reference is retained for a separate source audit.",
    "duas.content.367": "Surah occurs only in the inline reference, which is retained verbatim in English per the skill. Do not add an Urdu surah label to the narrative solely for the glossary check.",
    "duas.note.368": "English duplicates the rooster narration in the second paragraph. Bengali and the actual second reference, Abu Dawud 5103, concern dogs and donkeys at night; Urdu follows those, retaining [1] and [2]. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5103 .",
    "duas.translation.370": "English Messenger is singular, whereas the supplied Arabic rusulihi and Bengali are plural. Urdu correctly says His messengers.",
    "duas.note.372": "Abu Zumayl is the intermediary narrator reporting his question to Ibn Abbas, not a Companion. Urdu uses rahimahullah for him and radiyallahu anhuma for Ibn Abbas. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5110 .",
    "duas.translation.379": "English repent for me is incorrect for tub alayya, which asks Allah to accept repentance. It also swaps the wrong divine name: supplied Arabic and Bengali replace Rahim with Ghafur while retaining Tawwab.",
    "duas.note.380": "English middle of the night omits the qualifying last part. Bengali and Arabic Tirmidhi 3579 say the last part of the night. The heart wording follows the restrained covering metaphor also used in row 389. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3579 .",
    "duas.content.387": "English pray is imprecise: Bengali and the repeated Bukhari 6307 wording ask forgiveness and repent. Urdu explicitly preserves both actions.",
    "duas.content.388": "Arabic Muslim 2702b says al-Agharr was narrating TO Ibn Umar, not quoting FROM him. Abu Burdah is the intermediary narrator, so use rahimahullah. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2702b .",
    "duas.content.389": "English goes astray overstates the meaning. Bengali describes momentary preoccupation; Urdu preserves the covering metaphor of layughanu ala qalbi, matching the parallel narration in row 380. Arabic independently checked at https://sunnah.com/muslim:2702a .",
    "duas.content.390": "English wrongly introduces the displayed text as the prayer tashahhud. The supplied text is Khutbat al-Hajah, as Bengali says. Preserve the initial mention of both teachings but introduce the correct displayed passage.",
    "duas.translation.390": "English omits the kinship clause from Quran 4:1. Supplied Arabic wal-arham and Bengali both include it; Urdu restores it without altering citation numbers.",
    "duas.translation.394": "English and Bengali mistranslate the final clause as gathering or separating good things. Supplied Arabic asks Allah to keep the spouses together in goodness for as long as He joins them, and to separate them in goodness if He separates them.",
    "duas.translation.412": "English omits by Your favour, which is explicit in the supplied Arabic bifadlika and Bengali. Urdu preserves this phrase.",
    "duas.translation.416": "English repeats the grave trial and says wash my sins. Supplied Arabic and Bengali have one grave-trial clause and ask to wash the heart with snow and hail water. Urdu follows those without the English duplication.",
    "duas.translation.417": "English omits Lord of the earth, which appears in the supplied Arabic and Bengali. Restore it in Urdu and render the present grasp of the forelock rather than the English future tense.",
    "duas.note.365": "English reverses the wording of the hypothetical regret. Bengali and Muslim 2664 say if I had done such-and-such, this would have happened. Urdu preserves that conditional form.",
    "duas.note.381": "The prose omits the speaker. Musnad Ahmad 712 explicitly has Ali reporting that the Prophet addressed him; restore that attribution. Retain the unusual already-forgiven wording, which really occurs in the Arabic. Checked the Musnad text reproduced at https://dorar.net/h/JcEng0hJ?osoul=1 .",
    "duas.content.394": "The cited Adab al-Zifaf discusses a raised report but explicitly prefers the version stopping at Ibn Masud. Attribute this instruction to Ibn Masud rather than unconditionally to the Prophet; frozen reference remains unchanged. Checked https://islamhouse.com/read/ar/????-??????-??-?????-???????-276162 , section 2, footnote to the second report.",
    "duas.note.397": "The supplied claim about Companions conflicts with the Hasan al-Basri attribution in row 396 and the Nawawi recommendation for the reply in row 362. Urdu uses the accurate broader attribution to scholars; see Hisn al-Muslim chapter 47, https://risala.prh.gov.sa/storage/contents/51/ar_hisnulmuslim.pdf .",
    "duas.note.428": "English reverses the hypothetical by saying 'if I had not done that'. The supplied Arabic in Muslim 2664 says law anni fa'altu, and Bengali likewise says 'if I had done'; Urdu follows that wording, consistent with row 365. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2664 .",
    "duas.content.445": "English says Allah will forgive the debt. Bengali says He will free the person from debt, which is the intended meaning in this debt-settlement context; Urdu says Allah will grant release from debt.",
    "duas.translation.451": "English paraphrases wallahu hasibuhu as Allah knowing the exact truth. The supplied Arabic literally makes Allah the person's Reckoner; Urdu preserves that meaning.",
    "duas.group_items.453.1.content": "The malformed English changes the addressee and speaker. Muslim 2346 has people asking Abdullah ibn Sarjis whether the Messenger sought forgiveness for him; Abdullah answers yes, for them too, and recites the verse. Urdu restores those speakers. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2346 .",
    "duas.content.458": "English compresses Sa'd's offer into half his family and property. Bukhari 5167 says Sa'd ibn al-Rabi offered half his property and one of his two wives after divorce; Urdu states the actual offer without the misleading half-family wording. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5167 .",
    "duas.note.458": "English gives two awkward alternatives for the mahr. Bukhari 5167 states gold equal to the weight of a date stone; Urdu uses that exact meaning. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5167 .",
    "duas.content.463": "English accidentally repeats returning the greeting, creating six rights after announcing five. Bengali and Bukhari 1240 contain exactly five; Urdu removes the duplicate and preserves those five. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1240 .",
    "duas.content.469": "English is grammatically malformed and makes the listener the possible speaker. Tirmidhi 2741 explicitly instructs the person who sneezes to say this praise; Urdu restores that speaker. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2741 .",
    "duas.content.471": "English is grammatically malformed and appears to make the sneezer say yarhamukallah. Tirmidhi 2741 has another person say it to the sneezer, who then gives the displayed reply; Urdu makes the exchange explicit. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2741 .",
    "duas.translation.478": "As in row 451, supplied Arabic wallahu hasibuhu makes Allah the person's Reckoner. Urdu preserves that wording instead of the looser English paraphrase.",
    "duas.translation.483": "English mistranslates qurbatan as the reward of a sacrificial slaughter. The supplied Arabic, Bengali and Bukhari 6361 say a means of nearness to Allah; Urdu restores that meaning, consistent with row 450. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6361 .",
    "duas.translation.491": "English adds Paradise to 'make it a treasure for me'. The supplied Arabic indaka and Bengali say 'with You'; Urdu follows them. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3424 .",
    "duas.content.492": "English renders Arabic tiratan mechanically as deprivation descending. Bengali gives regret; Urdu uses the natural hadith sense, 'a cause of regret from Allah', for both sitting and lying. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4856 .",
    "duas.translation.494": "English says All-Forgiving, but the supplied Arabic ends al-Rahim and Bengali says Merciful. Urdu therefore uses 'Most Merciful' rather than repeating row 474, whose Arabic ends al-Ghafur.",
    "duas.content.497": "The English ending is badly corrupted. Urdu restores the instruction to eat with the right hand and from what is directly in front, followed by Umar ibn Abi Salamah's statement that he continued eating that way. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5376 .",
    "duas.name.501": "English says the dua is between eating and drinking. Muslim 2734a says Allah is pleased when a servant praises Him after eating food or drinking; Urdu corrects the timing. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2734a .",
    "duas.content.501": "Same timing correction as the title: praise follows eating or drinking, rather than occurring between them. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2734a .",
    "duas.content.511": "English corrupts the opening instruction. Bukhari 3304 says to keep children close when night begins because devils spread, then release them after part of the night has passed; Urdu restores that wording. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3304 .",
    "duas.note.512": "English has the nonsensical phrase 'donkeys of dogs'. Abu Dawud 5103 says dogs barking and donkeys braying at night; Urdu restores both animals and the reason for seeking refuge. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5103 .",
    "duas.translation.513": "English omits la ilaha illa anta, which is present in the supplied Arabic and Bengali. Urdu restores 'there is no deity worthy of worship except You'.",
    "duas.content.516": "English calls the wind Allah's 'liveliness'. Abu Dawud 5097 describes wind as being from Allah's mercy; Urdu follows the hadith. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5097 .",
    "duas.content.518": "English leaves the first-person narrator unnamed. Bukhari 3206 identifies her as Aisha; Urdu names her so the narration and direct address remain clear. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3206 .",
    "duas.translation.523": "English uses 'pardon us' for wa aafina. The supplied Arabic asks for well-being or safety; Urdu uses ├ÿ┬╣├ÿ┬º├Ö┬ü├¢┼Æ├ÿ┬¬ ├ÿ┬╣├ÿ┬╖├ÿ┬º ├Ö┬ü├ÿ┬▒├ÖΓÇª├ÿ┬º.",
    "duas.translation.524": "English mistranslates the opening as reliance. The supplied Arabic la tayra illa tayruka and Bengali concern omens; Urdu states that no omen has effect apart from Allah's decree.",
    "duas.note.524": "English omits the statement that gives the expiation its context. The supplied Bengali and Musnad Ahmad 7045 state that allowing an omen to stop an intended action is shirk; Urdu restores that sentence before the Companions' question.",
    "duas.note.531": "English labels al-Aswad with RA, but al-Aswad ibn Yazid is the intermediary narrator asking Aisha. Urdu uses rahimahullah for him while retaining radiyallahu anha for Aisha. The chain is visible in https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5741 .",
    "duas.translation.535": "English omits bi-idhni rabbina. The supplied Bengali and Bukhari 5745 include healing by permission of our Lord; Urdu restores that clause. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5745 .",
    "duas.group_items.536.0.note": "English says Uthman ibn Abi al-As reported an 'explanation' of his body. Muslim 2202 records his complaint of pain; Urdu restores the complaint and the Prophet's instructions. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2202 .",
    "duas.content.538": "English misidentifies the opening transmitters as Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Layla and his father. The cited Tirmidhi 969 has Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah narrating from his father; Urdu follows that chain and the cited report rather than the extra clauses in Bengali. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:969 .",
    "duas.content.544": "English names only Abu Hurayrah, but Tirmidhi 3430 has al-Agharr Abu Muslim bearing witness from both Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah. Urdu restores both Companion narrators. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3430 .",
    "duas.group_items.544.3.note": "The malformed English makes Allah the speaker of the concluding promise. Tirmidhi 3430 first gives Allah's affirmation, then attributes 'whoever says it during illness...' to the Prophet. Urdu makes both speakers explicit. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3430 .",
    "duas.content.546": "English omits whom to prompt and is grammatically incomplete. Muslim 916a says to prompt those who are dying to recite the declaration of faith; Urdu restores the object. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:916a .",
    "duas.note.4": "Surah occurs only in the inline citation, which remains normalized English under the project rules. Do not add an Urdu surah label solely to satisfy the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.translation.5": "English ends with 'You are upon a straight path', but the supplied Arabic and Bengali say that Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path. Urdu follows them.",
    "duas.translation.9": "English renders wa aafini as 'strengthen me'. The supplied Arabic and Bengali ask for well-being; Urdu correctly uses ├ÿ┬╣├ÿ┬º├Ö┬ü├¢┼Æ├ÿ┬¬.",
    "duas.translation.11": "English begins 'O Allah', but the supplied Arabic says Rabbi and Bengali likewise addresses 'my Lord'. Urdu follows the actual invocation: ├ÿ┬º├¢ΓÇÖ ├ÖΓÇª├¢┼Æ├ÿ┬▒├¢ΓÇÖ ├ÿ┬▒├ÿ┬¿.",
    "duas.note.13": "English renders dandanah as reciting beautifully. Ibn Majah 910 describes the man's inability to make the Prophet's and Muadh's detailed supplications and the reply that their supplication revolves around seeking Paradise and refuge from Hell; Urdu restores that sense. Checked https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:910 .",
    "duas.content.14": "English says one day, but the supplied Bengali says after some days and the Arabic of Tirmidhi 3514 has ayyaman. Urdu uses 'after a few days'. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3514 .",
    "duas.group_items.29.0.translation": "English omits wa aafini, although it is present in the supplied nested Arabic. Urdu restores the request for well-being.",
    "duas.content.30": "English omits that the new Muslim was first taught the prayer. The supplied Bengali and Muslim 2697b include this before the instruction to supplicate; Urdu restores it. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2697b .",
    "duas.translation.30": "English omits wa aafini, which is present in the supplied Arabic, Bengali and Muslim 2697b. Urdu restores 'grant me well-being'. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2697b .",
    "duas.name.254": "Surah occurs only inside the parenthetical Quran citation. The citation remains in English under the project rules, so no Urdu surah label is added solely for the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.translation.281": "Surah occurs only inside the inline Quran citation. The citation remains in English under the project rules, so no Urdu surah label is added solely for the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.note.496": "Tirmidhi occurs only inside the inline hadith citation. The citation remains in English under the project rules, so no Urdu collection name is added solely for the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.content.33": "English incorrectly gives Ibn Qudamah the Companion honorific RA. He is one of the transmitters whose version specifies the right hand; Urdu uses rahimahullah. Checked the chain at https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1502 .",
    "duas.content.38": "English says 'on the last night', but the cited Tirmidhi narration refers to the latter part of the night. Urdu states the intended time clearly.",
    "duas.translation.47": "English loosely says 'take me out of my plight'. The supplied Arabic ajurni fi musibati asks for reward in the calamity, and wakhluf li khayran minha asks for a better replacement; Urdu preserves both clauses.",
    "duas.note.49": "English mechanically renders the Prophet's question as 'such and such a word'. In context he asks who uttered the displayed words; Urdu makes that referent explicit. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:601 .",
    "duas.content.59": "English omits 'and the Prophets before me'. The supplied Bengali and Tirmidhi 3585 both include this clause; Urdu restores it. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3585 .",
    "duas.content.63": "English incorrectly begins with Umm Darda as narrator while continuing in Safwan's first person, and labels Safwan RA. The actual chain has Safwan ibn Abdullah narrating his exchange with Umm Darda; Urdu restores the speaker and uses rahimahullah for Safwan. The same chain is visible at https://sunnah.com/adab/31/22 .",
    "duas.note.65": "English labels the sub-narrator Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr with RA. He is a later transmitter, so Urdu uses rahimahullah. The wording about small girls is retained accurately. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:755 .",
    "duas.content.66": "English says the fasting person's supplication is accepted when he breaks his fast, but the supplied Bengali and the Arabic hatta yuftir in Tirmidhi 3598 say until he breaks his fast. Urdu follows the Arabic timing. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3598 .",
    "duas.name.69": "English calls this the oppressed person's supplication, but the content is Quran 27:62 about the desperate or distressed person. Urdu follows the actual verse subject.",
    "duas.translation.73": "As in row 47, English omits the explicit request for reward in the calamity. The supplied Arabic and Bengali include it; Urdu restores that meaning.",
    "duas.name.77": "English calls this the excellence of dua, but the report itself concerns sitting with people remembering Allah, and Bengali likewise identifies dhikr. Urdu names the actual subject.",
    "duas.translation.83": "English incorrectly asks for the good of this day. The supplied Arabic says hadhihi al-laylah and the evening context requires night; Urdu follows the Arabic.",
    "duas.translation.89": "English incorrectly says All-Seeing. The supplied Arabic al-Sami and the English note both say All-Hearing; Urdu follows the Arabic.",
    "duas.name.93": "English title says morning and evening, but the instruction and report specify reciting this in the morning. Urdu names the actual time.",
    "duas.note.100": "English confuses Abu Bakrah with Abu Bakr and labels his son as a Companion. Abu Dawud 5090 has Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah addressing his father Abu Bakrah; Urdu restores the names and uses rahimahullah for the intermediary. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5090 .",
    "duas.note.111": "English gives only the kunyah Abu Malik. Sahih Muslim 2697b and its narrator chain identify him as Sa'd ibn Tariq al-Ashja'i narrating from his Companion father Tariq ibn Ashyam; Urdu supplies their names and correct honorifics. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2697b and https://sunnah.com/narrator/3248 ."
  },

# Natural Urdu standard

Write contemporary, educated Pakistani Urdu suitable for worship, guidance, and general app screens. It should sound authored in Urdu, not converted sentence by sentence from English or Bengali.

## Voice

- Use calm, respectful, devotional language without artificial grandeur.
- Prefer familiar, flowing Urdu sentence order. Break unwieldy source sentences where meaning and markup permit.
- Address the reader consistently and respectfully; avoid casual `╪¬┘à` unless a quoted source requires it.
- Use idiomatic verbs and complete predicates. Avoid noun-heavy calques and English-style passive chains.
- Use common Urdu vocabulary where it is precise. Retain established Islamic Arabic terms rather than replacing them with Hindi/Sanskrit or awkward explanatory phrases.
- Do not add sermons, rulings, praise, or explanations absent from the source.

## Religious wording

- Use `╪º┘ä┘ä█ü` consistently, not variant spellings.
- Use `╪»╪╣╪º`, `╪░┌⌐╪▒`, `╪º╪░┌⌐╪º╪▒`, `┘å┘à╪º╪▓`, `╪▒┌⌐┘ê╪╣`, `╪│╪¼╪»█ü`, `╪¬┘ê╪¿█ü`, `╪º╪│╪¬╪║┘ü╪º╪▒`, `╪▒┘é█î█ü` according to the glossary.

- Use established Urdu spellings for prophets, Companions, scholars, surahs, collections, and places. Keep one spelling throughout.
- Translate the meaning of Quran/hadith prose faithfully while leaving Arabic fields and Arabic blocks untouched.

## Human-quality rejection signs

Rewrite text that has any of these traits:

- source-language word order, repeated pronouns, or stiff literal connectors;
- unnecessary English words when natural Urdu exists;
- Bengali script or Bengali grammatical structure;
- mixed respectful and casual address;
- incorrect gender, number, agreement, postpositions, or compound verbs;
- excessive Persianized formality that obscures a simple source;
- machine-like repetition, fragmented clauses, or untranslated labels;
- a title that names a different action/person/time from its content;
- numbers interpreted as dates, ages, or quantities not present in the source.

## Review aloud

After semantic comparison, read each target as continuous Urdu without looking at the source. It must be immediately understandable, grammatically complete, and natural when spoken. Then compare again with the source to ensure fluency did not remove qualifications, negation, speakers, references, or repetitions.

Keep ASCII digits in references and technical identifiers. Keep inline citations in normalized English unless the project glossary explicitly defines a different approved presentation.

Checked https://islamhouse.com/read/ar/????-??????-??-?????-???????-276162 , section 2, footnote to the second report.",
    "duas.note.397": "The supplied claim about Companions conflicts with the Hasan al-Basri attribution in row 396 and the Nawawi recommendation for the reply in row 362. Urdu uses the accurate broader attribution to scholars; see Hisn al-Muslim chapter 47, https://risala.prh.gov.sa/storage/contents/51/ar_hisnulmuslim.pdf .",
    "duas.note.428": "English reverses the hypothetical by saying 'if I had not done that'. The supplied Arabic in Muslim 2664 says law anni fa'altu, and Bengali likewise says 'if I had done'; Urdu follows that wording, consistent with row 365. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2664 .",
    "duas.content.445": "English says Allah will forgive the debt. Bengali says He will free the person from debt, which is the intended meaning in this debt-settlement context; Urdu says Allah will grant release from debt.",
    "duas.translation.451": "English paraphrases wallahu hasibuhu as Allah knowing the exact truth. The supplied Arabic literally makes Allah the person's Reckoner; Urdu preserves that meaning.",
    "duas.group_items.453.1.content": "The malformed English changes the addressee and speaker. Muslim 2346 has people asking Abdullah ibn Sarjis whether the Messenger sought forgiveness for him; Abdullah answers yes, for them too, and recites the verse. Urdu restores those speakers. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2346 .",
    "duas.content.458": "English compresses Sa'd's offer into half his family and property. Bukhari 5167 says Sa'd ibn al-Rabi offered half his property and one of his two wives after divorce; Urdu states the actual offer without the misleading half-family wording. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5167 .",
    "duas.note.458": "English gives two awkward alternatives for the mahr. Bukhari 5167 states gold equal to the weight of a date stone; Urdu uses that exact meaning. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5167 .",
    "duas.content.463": "English accidentally repeats returning the greeting, creating six rights after announcing five. Bengali and Bukhari 1240 contain exactly five; Urdu removes the duplicate and preserves those five. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1240 .",
    "duas.content.469": "English is grammatically malformed and makes the listener the possible speaker. Tirmidhi 2741 explicitly instructs the person who sneezes to say this praise; Urdu restores that speaker. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2741 .",
    "duas.content.471": "English is grammatically malformed and appears to make the sneezer say yarhamukallah. Tirmidhi 2741 has another person say it to the sneezer, who then gives the displayed reply; Urdu makes the exchange explicit. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2741 .",
    "duas.translation.478": "As in row 451, supplied Arabic wallahu hasibuhu makes Allah the person's Reckoner. Urdu preserves that wording instead of the looser English paraphrase.",
    "duas.translation.483": "English mistranslates qurbatan as the reward of a sacrificial slaughter. The supplied Arabic, Bengali and Bukhari 6361 say a means of nearness to Allah; Urdu restores that meaning, consistent with row 450. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6361 .",
    "duas.translation.491": "English adds Paradise to 'make it a treasure for me'. The supplied Arabic indaka and Bengali say 'with You'; Urdu follows them. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3424 .",
    "duas.content.492": "English renders Arabic tiratan mechanically as deprivation descending. Bengali gives regret; Urdu uses the natural hadith sense, 'a cause of regret from Allah', for both sitting and lying. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4856 .",
    "duas.translation.494": "English says All-Forgiving, but the supplied Arabic ends al-Rahim and Bengali says Merciful. Urdu therefore uses 'Most Merciful' rather than repeating row 474, whose Arabic ends al-Ghafur.",
    "duas.content.497": "The English ending is badly corrupted. Urdu restores the instruction to eat with the right hand and from what is directly in front, followed by Umar ibn Abi Salamah's statement that he continued eating that way. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5376 .",
    "duas.name.501": "English says the dua is between eating and drinking. Muslim 2734a says Allah is pleased when a servant praises Him after eating food or drinking; Urdu corrects the timing. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2734a .",
    "duas.content.501": "Same timing correction as the title: praise follows eating or drinking, rather than occurring between them. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2734a .",
    "duas.content.511": "English corrupts the opening instruction. Bukhari 3304 says to keep children close when night begins because devils spread, then release them after part of the night has passed; Urdu restores that wording. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3304 .",
    "duas.note.512": "English has the nonsensical phrase 'donkeys of dogs'. Abu Dawud 5103 says dogs barking and donkeys braying at night; Urdu restores both animals and the reason for seeking refuge. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5103 .",
    "duas.translation.513": "English omits la ilaha illa anta, which is present in the supplied Arabic and Bengali. Urdu restores 'there is no deity worthy of worship except You'.",
    "duas.content.516": "English calls the wind Allah's 'liveliness'. Abu Dawud 5097 describes wind as being from Allah's mercy; Urdu follows the hadith. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5097 .",
    "duas.content.518": "English leaves the first-person narrator unnamed. Bukhari 3206 identifies her as Aisha; Urdu names her so the narration and direct address remain clear. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3206 .",
    "duas.translation.523": "English uses 'pardon us' for wa aafina. The supplied Arabic asks for well-being or safety; Urdu uses ╪╣╪º┘ü█î╪¬ ╪╣╪╖╪º ┘ü╪▒┘à╪º.",
    "duas.translation.524": "English mistranslates the opening as reliance. The supplied Arabic la tayra illa tayruka and Bengali concern omens; Urdu states that no omen has effect apart from Allah's decree.",
    "duas.note.524": "English omits the statement that gives the expiation its context. The supplied Bengali and Musnad Ahmad 7045 state that allowing an omen to stop an intended action is shirk; Urdu restores that sentence before the Companions' question.",
    "duas.note.531": "English labels al-Aswad with RA, but al-Aswad ibn Yazid is the intermediary narrator asking Aisha. Urdu uses rahimahullah for him while retaining radiyallahu anha for Aisha. The chain is visible in https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5741 .",
    "duas.translation.535": "English omits bi-idhni rabbina. The supplied Bengali and Bukhari 5745 include healing by permission of our Lord; Urdu restores that clause. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5745 .",
    "duas.group_items.536.0.note": "English says Uthman ibn Abi al-As reported an 'explanation' of his body. Muslim 2202 records his complaint of pain; Urdu restores the complaint and the Prophet's instructions. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2202 .",
    "duas.content.538": "English misidentifies the opening transmitters as Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Layla and his father. The cited Tirmidhi 969 has Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah narrating from his father; Urdu follows that chain and the cited report rather than the extra clauses in Bengali. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:969 .",
    "duas.content.544": "English names only Abu Hurayrah, but Tirmidhi 3430 has al-Agharr Abu Muslim bearing witness from both Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah. Urdu restores both Companion narrators. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3430 .",
    "duas.group_items.544.3.note": "The malformed English makes Allah the speaker of the concluding promise. Tirmidhi 3430 first gives Allah's affirmation, then attributes 'whoever says it during illness...' to the Prophet. Urdu makes both speakers explicit. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3430 .",
    "duas.content.546": "English omits whom to prompt and is grammatically incomplete. Muslim 916a says to prompt those who are dying to recite the declaration of faith; Urdu restores the object. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:916a .",
    "duas.note.4": "Surah occurs only in the inline citation, which remains normalized English under the project rules. Do not add an Urdu surah label solely to satisfy the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.translation.5": "English ends with 'You are upon a straight path', but the supplied Arabic and Bengali say that Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path. Urdu follows them.",
    "duas.translation.9": "English renders wa aafini as 'strengthen me'. The supplied Arabic and Bengali ask for well-being; Urdu correctly uses ╪╣╪º┘ü█î╪¬.",
    "duas.translation.11": "English begins 'O Allah', but the supplied Arabic says Rabbi and Bengali likewise addresses 'my Lord'. Urdu follows the actual invocation: ╪º█Æ ┘à█î╪▒█Æ ╪▒╪¿.",
    "duas.note.13": "English renders dandanah as reciting beautifully. Ibn Majah 910 describes the man's inability to make the Prophet's and Muadh's detailed supplications and the reply that their supplication revolves around seeking Paradise and refuge from Hell; Urdu restores that sense. Checked https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:910 .",
    "duas.content.14": "English says one day, but the supplied Bengali says after some days and the Arabic of Tirmidhi 3514 has ayyaman. Urdu uses 'after a few days'. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3514 .",
    "duas.group_items.29.0.translation": "English omits wa aafini, although it is present in the supplied nested Arabic. Urdu restores the request for well-being.",
    "duas.content.30": "English omits that the new Muslim was first taught the prayer. The supplied Bengali and Muslim 2697b include this before the instruction to supplicate; Urdu restores it. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2697b .",
    "duas.translation.30": "English omits wa aafini, which is present in the supplied Arabic, Bengali and Muslim 2697b. Urdu restores 'grant me well-being'. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2697b .",
    "duas.name.254": "Surah occurs only inside the parenthetical Quran citation. The citation remains in English under the project rules, so no Urdu surah label is added solely for the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.translation.281": "Surah occurs only inside the inline Quran citation. The citation remains in English under the project rules, so no Urdu surah label is added solely for the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.note.496": "Tirmidhi occurs only inside the inline hadith citation. The citation remains in English under the project rules, so no Urdu collection name is added solely for the canonical-term check.",
    "duas.content.33": "English incorrectly gives Ibn Qudamah the Companion honorific RA. He is one of the transmitters whose version specifies the right hand; Urdu uses rahimahullah. Checked the chain at https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1502 .",
    "duas.content.38": "English says 'on the last night', but the cited Tirmidhi narration refers to the latter part of the night. Urdu states the intended time clearly.",
    "duas.translation.47": "English loosely says 'take me out of my plight'. The supplied Arabic ajurni fi musibati asks for reward in the calamity, and wakhluf li khayran minha asks for a better replacement; Urdu preserves both clauses.",
    "duas.note.49": "English mechanically renders the Prophet's question as 'such and such a word'. In context he asks who uttered the displayed words; Urdu makes that referent explicit. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:601 .",
    "duas.content.59": "English omits 'and the Prophets before me'. The supplied Bengali and Tirmidhi 3585 both include this clause; Urdu restores it. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3585 .",
    "duas.content.63": "English incorrectly begins with Umm Darda as narrator while continuing in Safwan's first person, and labels Safwan RA. The actual chain has Safwan ibn Abdullah narrating his exchange with Umm Darda; Urdu restores the speaker and uses rahimahullah for Safwan. The same chain is visible at https://sunnah.com/adab/31/22 .",
    "duas.note.65": "English labels the sub-narrator Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr with RA. He is a later transmitter, so Urdu uses rahimahullah. The wording about small girls is retained accurately. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:755 .",
    "duas.content.66": "English says the fasting person's supplication is accepted when he breaks his fast, but the supplied Bengali and the Arabic hatta yuftir in Tirmidhi 3598 say until he breaks his fast. Urdu follows the Arabic timing. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3598 .",
    "duas.name.69": "English calls this the oppressed person's supplication, but the content is Quran 27:62 about the desperate or distressed person. Urdu follows the actual verse subject.",
    "duas.translation.73": "As in row 47, English omits the explicit request for reward in the calamity. The supplied Arabic and Bengali include it; Urdu restores that meaning.",
    "duas.name.77": "English calls this the excellence of dua, but the report itself concerns sitting with people remembering Allah, and Bengali likewise identifies dhikr. Urdu names the actual subject.",
    "duas.translation.83": "English incorrectly asks for the good of this day. The supplied Arabic says hadhihi al-laylah and the evening context requires night; Urdu follows the Arabic.",
    "duas.translation.89": "English incorrectly says All-Seeing. The supplied Arabic al-Sami and the English note both say All-Hearing; Urdu follows the Arabic.",
    "duas.name.93": "English title says morning and evening, but the instruction and report specify reciting this in the morning. Urdu names the actual time.",
    "duas.note.100": "English confuses Abu Bakrah with Abu Bakr and labels his son as a Companion. Abu Dawud 5090 has Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah addressing his father Abu Bakrah; Urdu restores the names and uses rahimahullah for the intermediary. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5090 .",
    "duas.note.111": "English gives only the kunyah Abu Malik. Sahih Muslim 2697b and its narrator chain identify him as Sa'd ibn Tariq al-Ashja'i narrating from his Companion father Tariq ibn Ashyam; Urdu supplies their names and correct honorifics. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2697b and https://sunnah.com/narrator/3248 ."
  },

180:        "content": "Waking up and performing ablution and reciting the last ten verses of Surah Ali-Imran:",
181:        "translation": "(190) Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding. (191) Who remember Allah while standing or sitting or [lying] on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], \"Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]; then protect us from the punishment of the Fire. (192) Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire -  You have disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers. (193) Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], 'Believe in your Lord,' and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and cause us to die with the righteous. (194) Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in [Your] promise.\" (195) And their Lord responded to them, \"Never will I allow to be lost the work of [any] worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another. So those who emigrated or were evicted from their homes or were harmed in My cause or fought or were killed -  I will surely remove from them their misdeeds, and I will surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow as reward from Allah, and Allah has with Him the best reward.\" (196) Be not deceived by the [uninhibited] movement of the disbelievers throughout the land. (197) [It is but] a small enjoyment; then their [final] refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place. (198) But those who feared their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein, as accommodation from Allah . And that which is with Allah is best for the righteous. (199) And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, [being] humbly submissive to Allah . They do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account. (200) O you who have believed, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful. (Sura Al-Imran 3: 190-200)",

179:        "name": "Dua when waking up at night #2",
180:        "content": "Waking up and performing ablution and reciting the last ten verses of Surah Ali-Imran:",
181:        "translation": "(190) Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding. (191) Who remember Allah while standing or sitting or [lying] on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], \"Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]; then protect us from the punishment of the Fire. (192) Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire -  You have disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers. (193) Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], 'Believe in your Lord,' and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and cause us to die with the righteous. (194) Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in [Your] promise.\" (195) And their Lord responded to them, \"Never will I allow to be lost the work of [any] worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another. So those who emigrated or were evicted from their homes or were harmed in My cause or fought or were killed -  I will surely remove from them their misdeeds, and I will surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow as reward from Allah, and Allah has with Him the best reward.\" (196) Be not deceived by the [uninhibited] movement of the disbelievers throughout the land. (197) [It is but] a small enjoyment; then their [final] refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place. (198) But those who feared their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein, as accommodation from Allah . And that which is with Allah is best for the righteous. (199) And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, [being] humbly submissive to Allah . They do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account. (200) O you who have believed, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful. (Sura Al-Imran 3: 190-200)",
